The sign-in screen is ready as a working mock (it doesn't store anything yet — it's just to confirm the *experience* is what you want). **Please open http://maker:4001/login.html.**

**First — signing in (the everyday case):**
This is what you'd see when you open the app on a device where you're not signed in. Type any email and password and click **Sign in**. Confirm the message that appears matches your expectation — that your links would then load, the same on every device.

**Then — the very first time (setting up):**
Click **"Create your account"** at the bottom. The screen switches to setting up your account (with a confirm-password field). Fill it in and click **Create account**.

A few things I decided that I'd like you to judge:

- **I chose email + password** as the way you identify yourself. Since it's just for you, that's the simplest thing that lets your links follow you. Does that feel right, or did you have another way of signing in in mind?
- **I added a "Keep me signed in on this device" option, ticked by default**, so you're not re-entering your password every time you open it on your own laptop or phone — you'd only sign in again if you sign out or use a new device. Is that the behaviour you'd want?
- I set it up so **there's one account — yours** — with a "create account" step the very first time, then plain sign-in afterwards.

Tell me how the sign-in and account-creation screens feel, and whether those three choices match what you pictured.
